newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh president packs up, says has no regrets.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh president packs up, says has no regrets.

text.p: Bangladesh President Abdur Rahman Biswas left the presidental palace in Dhaka on Tuesday, making way for Shahabuddin Ahmed who takes over on Wednesday.
Palace officials said the president had told his staff that he was leaving with "nothing to regret".
"I did what I thought was right. I acted democratically. I didn't fear anyone nor will I fear anyone in the future," one official quoted the president as saying.

"Shahabuddin Ahmed is a good man. I hope he will be able to strengthen democracy in this country," Biswas said. "How (effective) was I? It is for the people to judge. I am satisfied. I am leaving after serving a full term."

His successor, a retired chief justice, will be formally sworn in on Wednesday. Chief Justice Abu Taher Mohammad Afzal will administer the oath at the "Bangabhaban" presidential palace. Biswas will attend the ceremony.

Ahmed was elected by parliament in July for a five-year term. He earlier earned worldwide admiration and the respect of Bangladeshis after presiding over a free and fair election in 1991, which elected Begum Khaleda Zia, now leader of the ooposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), the country's first woman prime minister.
Ahmed was then Bangladesh's acting president, following the removal of former president Hossain Mohammad Ershad in a popular up rising.
Biswas was the first Bangladeshi president to serve his full five-year term in office after being appointed president on October 8 in 1991.
As a member of Khaleda's Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), he has often been criticised for alleged partisan behaviour.

"I have been criticised for no genuine cause. The former opposition Awami League (now the ruling party) had asked me to impose military rule while the country experienced a turbulent political campaign (over the last two years)," Biswas told his palace staff.
"But I didn't...because that would upset democracy. Now that they (the Awami League) are in power, they are criticising me for trying to destroy democracy," he said.
No one from Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's Awami League was immediately available for comment on Biswas' remarks.
